cohort: 1947 pregnant women in Wuhan (epicenter of COVID-19 outbreak) and Chongqing (a less affected city) in China
finding: The COVID-19 outbreak was associated with increased prenatal anxiety and changes in obstetric decision-making, particularly in the epicenter city.
mod_finding: Obstetric decision-making changes included preferences regarding hospital, timing of prenatal care and delivery, mode of delivery, and infant feeding.
